clue.text: What could produce minor hitch?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says to write the word draw backwards, which gives WARD, and a ward is a minor in someone's care

explanation.surface: Someone asking what might cause a small snag.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split in two, is a piece of wordplay whose result is WARD, a legal word for a minor under a guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or disadvantage is a hitch, the usual synonym pair.

clue.text: Cotton shrinking upset Yankee

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: shrinking, as in a shrinking violet, means timid
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American's cotton garment shrank in the wash and upset them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TIMID into DIMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a light, sheer fabric woven from cotton with raised stripes or checks.

clue.text: Minister going topless is a firing offence

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top letter, the first one in this down entry

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman stripping off would surely get him sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing offence' looks like a sackable act at work; it is literally a crime of setting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence, quite literally one of firing.

clue.text: Obstruction is brief? No way

indicators.note: no here means without, so the word for way is taken out

parts.note: brief is slang for a lawyer, specifically a barrister
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether an obstruction will be short, and being told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like an adjective, short; it is the noun, slang for a barrister, a courtroom lawyer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence or bar that blocks passage is an obstruction.

clue.text: Ate a cracking fish starter in restaurant, and to follow one beef dish

indicators.note: to follow says the word and comes after the numeral for one
cracking means breaking into, so the words ate a go inside the fish

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner eats a fish starter in a restaurant before moving on to a beef main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it is the container signal, breaking into the fish. 'to follow' is the order signal, nothing to do with the meal's next course.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick fillet steak cut from the tenderloin, served roasted or grilled, is a classic beef dish.

clue.text: Twice yearly wife provides fruit

indicators.note: twice says the two pieces together are written two times over

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, Latin for yearly

explanation.surface: A husband twice a year presents his wife with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree bearing a large edible fruit, also called papaya.

clue.text: Excuse given by a bishop on crack

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A bishop on drugs offers an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug; it is the verb, to work out a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from blame or duty is to free or pardon them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Crew heading off after year in stinking capital city

indicators.note: after says the shortened crew comes later in the answer
in says the abbreviation for year goes inside the word for stinking

parts.note: pongy is British slang for smelly, from pong, a stink

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a gang is a crew of people

explanation.surface: A ship's crew leaving port after a year in a foul-smelling city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the G from GANG, leaving ANG.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the seat of government of North Korea, its largest city.

clue.text: Backed minister to approve law, obtaining an easy victory

indicators.note: backed means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: REV, short for Reverend, is a minister
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: A clergyman supporting a new statute wins easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reverses REVOKLAW. 'Backed' looks like supported, as in backing a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest won without effort, originally a race where the winner merely had to walk the course.

clue.text: Varied crimes by worker? He must be one

definitions.text: Varied crimes by worker? He must be one

indicators.note: varied means the letters of the word crimes are changed around

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Someone committing all sorts of crimes must be a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' rearranges CRIMES to MISCRE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a worker of varied crimes must be a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or wrongdoer is someone who commits crimes of many kinds.

clue.text: Flexible new star learned to change characters

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: literate means well read, learned

explanation.surface: A new film star proves flexible and learns to play different characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flexible' rearranges N and STAR to TRANS. 'characters' looks like roles; it means letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This means writing words in the letters of another alphabet, swapping one set of written symbols for another.

clue.text: Small lake sinks lower and lower

indicators.note: sinks means the abbreviation for lake drops to the bottom of the string

parts.note: a cow lows, so it is a lower

explanation.surface: The water level in a small lake keeps falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is used twice: first as a cow, one that lows (moos), then as the definition, a verb meaning to look sullen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower, also spelt lour, is to frown or look menacing.

clue.text: Character pockets money for annuity scheme

indicators.note: pockets means takes inside, so the word for money is put within

parts.note: tone means character, as in the tone of a place
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A shady character pockets cash meant for a pension fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme where subscribers share an annuity, the survivors' shares growing as others die.

clue.text: Everyone I must restrain runs fast

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: restraining holds something in, so the abbreviation for runs goes inside

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Everyone, me included, must stop running so fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning to play briskly or at a lively tempo.

clue.text: Notorious libertine composed sad, sad requiem

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A notorious rake wrote a mournful mass for the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges SAD SAD REQUIEM; it looks like a composer writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: The French aristocrat writer whose name gave us sadism was infamous for debauchery.

clue.text: Procession of cars round Democrat on the move?

indicators.note: on the move means moving about, so these letters are shifted around

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cavalcade circles a Democrat politician on the campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges O and DEMOCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of cars travelling together, typically escorting a dignitary.

clue.text: So detective appears in long story divided into several parts

indicators.note: appears in says these pieces show up inside the word for a long story

parts.note: an epic is a long story
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective turns up in a lengthy serialised tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Told in instalments, like a drama in separate episodes.

clue.text: Learning for toddlers — a clue for Gran in it?

parts.words: a clue for Gran in it
parts.note: read as a clue, the answer is an anagram indicator, potty, beside a word whose letters rearrange to spell the words gran in it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what toddlers learn, with Granny somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'potty' means crazy, a familiar anagram signal, and the second word is an anagram of GRANINIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching small children to use a toilet is the lesson toddlers learn.

clue.text: Get any swimming around Zulu river?

indicators.note: around means the letters wrap around the code letter
swimming suggests movement, so these letters swirl into a new order

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Anyone going swimming around a Zulu in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges GET ANY to YANGTE, which goes 'around' Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in Asia, flowing across China to the East China Sea.

clue.text: The opposite of how Milton wrote?

definitions.meaning: the reverse or converse of something
Milton wrote poetry, so he composed in lines of metre

explanation.surface: A literary question contrasting Milton's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means in poetry; as one it means the reverse.

clue.text: Bit of loose skin covered up by Italian garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
covered means held inside, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: A bit of skin hidden beneath an Italian piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' finds LIANGA inside 'Italian garment'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangnail, the torn strip of skin at the side of a fingernail.

clue.text: Briefly spray a lilac

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to syringe a plant is to spray it with water

explanation.surface: A gardener gives a lilac a quick spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the last E from SYRINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for the lilac genus, also used of mock orange.

clue.text: Resenting competing alongside extremists in election

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: vying means competing

explanation.surface: A candidate bitter about rivals standing alongside extremists at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling envy towards someone means begrudging what they have.

clue.text: Images clicked on notebook's screen, first of all?

definitions.text: Images clicked on notebook's screen, first of all?

indicators.note: first of all means take the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Things a laptop user clicks on the display first.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five clue words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pictures on a computer screen that are clicked to open programs.

clue.text: Plan one leaving board in a huff announced?

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.words: one leaving board in a huff
parts.note: in the board game draughts (checkers), to huff is to take an opponent's piece as a penalty, so a piece leaves the board

explanation.surface: A director storms off the board, taking his plans with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a huff' looks like sulking; in draughts, the British name for checkers, huffing removes a piece. 'board' looks like a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary version of a document or scheme is a plan.

clue.text: Do I hear a tail-ender finally bats, getting the runs?

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters are scrambled
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator wonders whether a lower-order batsman is scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' rearranges DOIHEARA plus R. A tail-ender is a weak batsman at the end of a cricket batting order.
explanation.definitionFit: The runs is slang for a bout of loose bowels.

clue.text: Smart bar to east of Croatia's capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, to the east of means placed after, on the right
capital means the first letter of the word, at its head

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: A stylish bar east of Zagreb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city such as Zagreb; it is just the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of intelligent, quick-witted.

clue.text: It makes star pupils slip up? Rats!

definitions.text: It makes star pupils slip up? Rats!

parts.words: It makes star pupils slip up? Rats!
parts.note: turning words backwards turns rats into star and pupils into slip up, which is what the clue describes

explanation.surface: A teacher's dismay when top pupils make an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue's words backwards: RATS gives STAR, SLIPUP gives PUPILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnaround reading a word from end to start is this kind of reverse operation.
